content.caseIdentity: AIIMS Students’ Union v. AIIMS, (2002) 1 SCC 428; AIR 2001 SC 3262
content.facts: The Supreme Court considered institutional reservation/preference in postgraduate medical admissions at AIIMS and the constitutional requirements of equality and merit.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether institutional reservation/source preference in postgraduate medical admissions is constitutionally permissible.
How Article 14 and merit constrain admission preferences.
content.ratioDecidendi: The Court distinguished a limited source preference from excessive institutional reservation and emphasized equality, merit, rational nexus and non-dilution of academic standards.
content.holding: The challenged admission arrangement was subjected to constitutional equality and merit principles; excessive institutional reservation was not sustainable merely by labeling it a separate source.
content.relevance: Leading authority on institutional preference, merit and equality in professional education.
